cards.info: How do you calculate the mean of a data set?
cards.backInfo: Add all values together and divide by the total number of values.

cards.info: What is the first step to determine the median?
cards.backInfo: Arrange the data set in order from least to greatest or greatest to least.

cards.info: How is the median determined for an even number of values?
cards.backInfo: Take the arithmetic average of the two middle values.

cards.info: What is the definition of the mode?
cards.backInfo: The value that appears most frequently in a data set.

cards.info: How do you calculate the range of a data set?
cards.backInfo: Subtract the minimum value from the maximum value.

cards.info: What is the definition of the first quartile ($Q_1$)?
cards.backInfo: The median of the lower half of an ordered data set.

cards.info: What is the formula for the interquartile range (IQR)?
Which is less affected by outliers: the mean or the median?
cards.backInfo: The median is less affected by extreme values (outliers).

cards.info: What part of the data spread does the IQR measure?
cards.backInfo: The spread of the middle 50% of the data.

cards.info: How is the numerator handled when calculating mean from a frequency table?
cards.backInfo: Multiply each value by its frequency and sum the results.

cards.info: How is the third quartile ($Q_3$) defined?
cards.backInfo: The median of the upper half of an ordered data set.

cards.info: If all values in a set are equal, what are the range and IQR?
cards.backInfo: Both the range and the interquartile range (IQR) are 0.

cards.info: In the mean formula $\text{Mean} = (\sum x) / n$, what does $n$ represent?
cards.backInfo: $n$ represents the total number of values in the data set.

cards.info: What error occurs if you calculate the median without sorting the data?
cards.backInfo: You incorrectly identify the middle value of the unsorted sequence as the median.

cards.info: For a set of 6 numbers, the median is the average of which positions?
cards.backInfo: The arithmetic average of the 3rd and 4th values.

cards.info: Must a data set have exactly one mode?
cards.backInfo: No, it can have one mode, multiple modes, or no mode.

cards.info: What characteristic of a data set does the range reflect?
cards.backInfo: It reflects the total span (difference between max and min values).

cards.info: When calculating $Q_1$, which part of the data is used?
cards.backInfo: The lower half of the ordered data set.

cards.info: Why is the median often better than the mean when outliers exist?
cards.backInfo: Because the median is not sensitive to extreme values and is more robust.

cards.info: What goes in the denominator when calculating mean from a frequency table?
cards.backInfo: The sum of all frequencies for all values.
